metaData.originalTitle: Automated Schema Evolution in Pinterest’s Next-Generation DB Ingestion Framework
metaData.title: Automated Schema Evolution in Pinterest’s Next-Generation DB Ingestion Framework
metaData.oneSentenceSummary: This article details how Pinterest built an automated schema evolution framework for its CDC-based ingestion pipeline, using a staged convergence model to safely propagate additive schema changes across Kafka, Flink, Spark, and Iceberg.
metaData.summary: The post is the second in a series on Pinterest's next-generation DB ingestion platform. It addresses the challenge of schema evolution in a distributed CDC pipeline where schema is a cross-system contract. The authors describe their solution: an automated framework that supports additive schema changes (column additions and precision widening) through a three-phase convergence model — schema divergence first (updating Iceberg schemas while existing jobs continue), code convergence (deploying updated Flink and Spark logic), and data convergence (backfilling via Spark). Changes are detected through push-based (DDL CDC messages) and pull-based (daily comparison) mechanisms, and all updates go through PR-based workflow for auditability. The system explicitly handles edge cases like columns with defaults, sensitive data changes, ambiguous CREATE TABLE diffs, and concurrent changes. Observability metrics at pipeline and data level ensure convergence is tracked. The article concludes with a vision for zero-gap schema evolution using a dynamic Iceberg sink, and notes the current limitations (needs Flink version bump).

mainPoints.point: Schema evolution is a cross-system contract, not just metadata.
mainPoints.explanation: A single upstream schema change must propagate consistently across Kafka, Flink, Spark, and Iceberg, affecting code, metadata, and storage. Treating it as a contract enables systematic automation.

mainPoints.point: Automated schema evolution is restricted to additive changes for safety.
mainPoints.explanation: Only column additions and numeric precision widening are supported automatically. This preserves backward compatibility, avoids historical replay complexity, and minimizes consumer breakage.

mainPoints.point: A three-phase convergence model decouples schema updates from data correctness.
mainPoints.explanation: Iceberg schemas are updated first (phase 1), then Flink/Spark code (phase 2), then backfill (phase 3). Temporary divergence is bounded by SLA, ensuring pipeline availability while restoring consistency.

mainPoints.point: Push-based and pull-based detection mechanisms complement each other.
mainPoints.explanation: DDL CDC messages trigger immediate evolution (push), while a daily comparison job catches missed changes (pull). This combination provides low latency with a safety net.

keyQuotes: schema is not just metadata --- it is a cross-system contract spanning ingestion, transformation, storage, and historical backfill.
A key design principle is that schema evolution is not treated as an atomic operation. Instead, we treat it as a multi-stage convergence process across the control plane and data plane.

This staged approach decouples schema propagation from data correctness. Instead of forcing the entire system to change atomically, we allow temporary divergence within a bounded SLA and use deployment sequencing to restore full consistency.

relatedArticles.title: Designing Data-intensive Applications with Martin Kleppmann
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: In this podcast interview, Martin Kleppmann, author of 'Designing Data-Intensive Applications,' discusses the book's second edition, his experiences at LinkedIn with Kafka, the evolving challenges of cloud-native architecture, the growing importance of formal verification in the AI era, and his current academic research on local-first software and supply chain cryptography.

relatedArticles.title: How OpenAI Built Its Data Agent
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article details how OpenAI's data platform team built a simple, reliable data agent by focusing on a strong data infrastructure foundation and a rich context assembly layer, rather than a complex agent architecture.

relatedArticles.title: From Batch to Micro-Batch Streaming: Lessons Learned the Hard Way in a Delta Index Pipeline
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article details the migration of a batch-oriented delta index pipeline to a micro-batch streaming model, emphasizing that eliminating scheduling delays and adopting deterministic, freshness-driven progress is more valuable than pursuing record-level streaming.

relatedArticles.title: How to Build an Open Source Data Lake for Batch Ingestion
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article provides a comprehensive, hands-on tutorial for building a modern, open-source data lake ingestion layer using RustFS, Apache Iceberg, Project Nessie, Apache Spark, and Airflow, complete with a decoupled web scraper pattern.

relatedArticles.title: From Clicks to Conversions: Architecting Shopping Conversion Candidate Generation at Pinterest
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article details Pinterest Engineering's journey in building a dedicated shopping conversion candidate generation model, from training data design and feature engineering to novel parallel DCN v2 and unified multi-task architectures, achieving significant lifts in conversion volume and RoAS.

relatedArticles.title: Performance for Everyone: Automating User Perceived Latency Measurement at Pinterest
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Pinterest engineering shares an automated approach to measuring 'Visually Complete' latency by integrating performance tracking directly into the base UI class, significantly reducing engineering overhead.

relatedArticles.title: Optimizing ML Workload Network Efficiency (Part I): Feature Trimmer
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Pinterest Engineering shares how they solved a network bottleneck in their ML serving system by implementing a 'Feature Trimmer' that sends only the features each model actually uses, reducing root-leaf network bandwidth by up to 75% and saving over $4M annually.

relatedArticles.title: Enhancing Ad Relevance: Integrating Real-Time Context into Sequential Recommender Models
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Pinterest Engineering details the development of a Contextual Sequential Two-Tower Model that integrates real-time browsing context into ad candidate generation, achieving a 3x to 10x improvement in recall and a ~275-300% increase in candidate relevance on the Related Pins surface.

relatedArticles.title: Beyond Prompting: Context Engineering and Memory Management for AI Systems at Scale
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This talk by Adi Polak argues that building effective AI systems at scale requires moving beyond prompt engineering to context engineering, which encompasses memory management, state management, and retrieval, using distributed systems like Kafka and Flink as the architectural foundation.

relatedArticles.title: Making User-Sequence Data More Cost-Efficient, Faster, and Easier to Use
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Pinterest Engineering redesigned its user-sequence platform with a 'one definition, many runtimes' architecture, configuration-as-code, a shared execution engine, and columnar storage to improve cost-efficiency, developer productivity, and data quality for ML models.
